title: Secure login and failed-login lockout
story: As an Admin or Student, I want secure email/password login so that I can access my role's workspace.
acceptance: Valid credentials issue a role-scoped JWT/session. After five consecutive failures, the sixth attempt is rejected for 15 minutes even with the correct password; the event is logged. Passwords use salted Argon2 or bcrypt and never appear in logs.

title: Enforce role permissions on every API
story: As a faculty administrator, I want server-enforced permissions so that students cannot modify administrative data.
acceptance: Student tokens receive 403 for every Admin-only route. Anonymous callers are rejected. Permission tests cover all implemented API routes and ownership boundaries.

title: Admin-triggered student password reset
story: As an Admin, I want to reset a student's password through email re-verification.
acceptance: Reset links expire after one hour and can be used once only. The student completes email re-verification; unauthorized users cannot initiate Admin reset operations.

title: Create and maintain MCQ questions
story: As an Admin, I want a reusable MCQ question bank with a usable React editing interface.
acceptance: Create, edit and delete questions with 2–6 options, exactly one correct option, marks, negative marks, subject, topic and difficulty. Reject zero or multiple correct options and invalid option counts on the server. Show validation errors in the UI.

title: Search and filter the question bank
story: As an Admin, I want to find questions by subject, topic and difficulty.
acceptance: Search/filter returns only matching questions, supports combined filters, and clearly displays no-match results in the UI.

title: Import students and manage batch membership
story: As an Admin, I want to import the student roster and organize students into batches.
acceptance: CSV/Excel import accepts name, email, USN and batch. Valid rows create accounts; invalid/duplicate rows are reported with reasons. Create batches/sections and support multiple batch memberships per student through a many-to-many relationship.

title: Create and schedule exams
story: As an Admin, I want to create and schedule an exam using a clear form.
acceptance: Persist title, duration, total marks, start time, end time and result-visible-from. Enforce end > start and valid duration. Keep total marks consistent with selected questions. Provide clear field validation errors.

title: Select exam questions manually or randomly
story: As an Admin, I want to build an exam from tagged question pools.
acceptance: Manual selection preserves question ordering. Random selection respects requested counts and difficulty mix, avoids duplicate questions and reports insufficient pools. Total marks are recomputed when exam questions change.

title: Assign exams to batches and show eligible exams
story: As a Student, I want to see only exams I am eligible to access.
acceptance: An Admin can assign an exam to one or more batches. Students see/access only exams assigned to their batches and within the scheduled window; direct API access outside those boundaries is rejected. Sprint 1 delivers eligible-exam listing; attempting is delivered in Sprint 2.

title: Keep answer keys confidential
story: As an exam coordinator, I want answer keys to remain confidential throughout the student journey.
acceptance: No Student-reachable API, page source or browser state contains correct-option flags or answer keys. Inspect attempt-question responses and test role-specific serializers. Evaluation reads keys only on the server. Apply the same rule to Sprint 1 endpoints; full attempt-path acceptance is Sprint 2.

title: Enforce one active attempt and session
story: As a Student, I want one recoverable exam attempt protected against concurrent sessions.
acceptance: Enforce uniqueness of exam/student attempts and separately bind an IN_PROGRESS attempt to one active session. Concurrent second-session access is rejected. Test race conditions and refresh/reconnect from the permitted session.

title: Autosave answers and recover after refresh
story: As a Student, I want my answers saved so that a refresh or client crash does not erase my work.
acceptance: Persist current answers at most 10 seconds apart and restore the last saved state after refresh/crash. Test recovered-state age and retry/backoff behavior. Report network failures honestly; document outages that prevent the 10-second guarantee.

title: Server timer and automatic submission
story: As a Student, I want a visible countdown and fair server-controlled submission.
acceptance: Render a persistent countdown based on the server deadline. At expiry the server transitions to AUTO_SUBMITTED even if the browser is inactive or closed. Reject late writes and verify client-clock changes cannot extend time. Manual submission is supported and idempotent.

title: Evaluate submissions and release results
story: As a Student, I want an accurate result released at the configured time.
acceptance: Server evaluation computes sum(correct marks) minus sum(incorrect negative marks); unanswered questions score zero. Produce one result per attempt; repeated submission does not duplicate scoring. Hide results until result_visible_from, including direct API requests.

title: Lock responses after submission
story: As an exam coordinator, I want submitted answers to remain immutable.
acceptance: Every write path rejects updates once status leaves IN_PROGRESS, including submitted, auto-submitted and disqualified attempts. Test concurrent save/submit races and unauthorized changes.

title: Class and question reports with exports
story: As an Admin, I want class and question-wise reports that I can export.
acceptance: Generate class-performance and question-difficulty reports; CSV and PDF totals match the on-screen report. Enforce role restrictions, result-release rules and disqualification exclusions.

title: Proctoring flags, overrides and audit trail
story: As an Admin, I want to review exam flags and make attributable decisions.
acceptance: Two tab switches produce two visible log entries; log window blur events. Admins can disqualify/re-permit flagged attempts and disqualified results stay excluded until re-permitted. All question edits and result/attempt overrides create append-only entries with actor, timestamp and action. Question-edit auditing begins in Sprint 1; full override acceptance is Sprint 2.

title: Schedule and result email notifications
story: As a Student, I want email alerts for scheduled exams and released results.
acceptance: Queue notifications to affected students within one minute of scheduling or result visibility. Test recipients, retries and duplicate prevention; retain queue/log evidence without exposing credentials.

title: HTTPS and protected session cookies
story: As a user, I want credentials and session traffic protected in transit.
acceptance: Deployment uses HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ and session/refresh cookies have HttpOnly and Secure attributes. Keep secrets outside source control. Provide TLS/cookie inspection evidence; local HTTP development does not count as deployed TLS acceptance.
tests: SRS TLS scan and cookie inspection; deployment checks

title: Input validation and injection defenses
story: As a user, I want malicious inputs rejected or safely rendered.
acceptance: Persist through parameterized ORM queries; validate user input server-side and safely render question text. Exercise SQL injection and stored-XSS payloads in search, question editing and import. Extend these checks to new Sprint 2 endpoints.

title: Performance and scaling verification
story: As an exam coordinator, I want the portal to support a full class concurrently.
acceptance: Attempt page loads within 2 seconds and supports 200 concurrent students with p95 response time no worse than 3 seconds. Application instances can scale horizontally with shared persistent state. Review attempt and response lookup indexes with EXPLAIN; document equivalent response indexing through attempt_id where required by schema.
tests: TC-Perf-01; design review and EXPLAIN evidence

title: Monitor availability during exam windows
story: As an exam coordinator, I want service availability measured during scheduled exams.
acceptance: Provide health checks and monitoring logs showing at least 99.5% availability over the stated published test-exam window, excluding announced maintenance. State the measurement interval and downtime calculation; do not claim semester-long reliability from a short run.

title: Responsive and accessible exam interface
story: As a Student, I want an exam interface usable on desktop, mobile and keyboard.
acceptance: Exam-taking screens support responsive viewports, keyboard navigation, labels/focus visibility and WCAG 2.1 AA basics including contrast. Record manual audit and Lighthouse score >=90. Apply foundational responsive styles in Sprint 1, then verify attempt screens in Sprint 2.

title: Core-module coverage and traceable test results
story: As the test team, we want measured coverage and requirement-linked evidence.
acceptance: CI measures at least 70% automated unit-test coverage for exam and evaluation engines. Maintain the full FR/NFR/SR RTM, actual pass/fail results, defects and a test summary. Do not mark requirements passed before execution.
tests: CI coverage report; Test Plan deliverables

title: Set up the documented application foundation
story: As a developer, I want a reproducible React/Django/PostgreSQL foundation.
acceptance: Document local setup, environment template, migrations and demo seed data. Use Django REST Framework APIs, React frontend and PostgreSQL per SAD; provide Docker configuration. Record any deviation explicitly. This story enables feature work and does not itself prove FR completion.

title: Sprint 1 CI, PRs and genuine reviews
story: As the team, we want repeatable checks and review evidence for Sprint 1.
acceptance: Run GitHub Actions on pushes and PRs, including backend/frontend checks and relevant tests. Link PRs to stories. The assigned team member raises their PR, and a real eligible reviewer reviews it. Record actual CI/review evidence; changes made through Chiranthan's connection must not be attributed to teammates.
tests: GitHub Actions runs and PR/review links

title: Sprint 1 working demo and evaluation evidence
story: As the team lead, I want a reproducible one-minute demonstration of completed Sprint 1 work.
acceptance: Record approximately 60 seconds of the actual working Sprint 1 product and upload the video to the repository. Include a short demo script, run instructions, completed-story/PR/test links and documented deviations. Do not substitute mock screens or claim unfinished stories are complete.
